cards.explanation: The answer is armies, friends. Jabin, king of Hazor, sent word to the other kings, and they "…came out with all their armies, a multitude as numerous as the sand on the seashore…" (Joshua 11:1, 4). Kings from the mountains, the foothills, the Arabah and beyond all showed up. You know how hard it is to get a whole family to agree on one dinner time? These kings got ALL those armies to one place!

The answer is the waters of Merom, friends. Verse 5 says the kings joined forces and encamped at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel. They all parked in one spot, and that spot is where the battle comes to them. Remember that name, because you'll see it again.

The answer is "Do not be afraid of them…" That's the very first thing the LORD says to Joshua. Look at the size of that army, then look at those words. The LORD gives Joshua a plan right after, so Joshua doesn't have to guess what comes next. When the LORD says don't be afraid, that settles it.

The answer is burn them up, friends. The LORD says, "You are to hamstring their horses and burn up their chariots." Verse 9 says Joshua did exactly that. The chariots go up in flames, so nobody gets them back.

The answer is False. Nothing in the text says Israel had more soldiers. The kings brought a multitude as numerous as the sand on the seashore (Joshua 11:4). Joshua 11:8 says the LORD delivered them into the hand of Israel. The battle was won by the LORD's hand, not by headcount.

The answer is True, friends! The LORD told Joshua to hamstring the horses and burn up the chariots (Joshua 11:6). Then verse 9 says Joshua treated them as the LORD had told him. No tweaking, no "close enough." I've been known to eyeball the flour and call it a day, so this kind of follow-through impresses me.

The answer is that Hazor had been the head of all these kingdoms. Verse 10 says Hazor "…was formerly the head of all these kingdoms." It was the top city of the bunch. So when Joshua turns back, he's going straight to the head.

The answer is that he captures them all, friends. Verse 12 says Joshua captured all these kings and their cities and put them to the sword. He devoted them to destruction, as Moses the LORD's servant had commanded. That's a big sweep, and it's a heavy part of the story.

The answer is True. Verse 13 says Israel did not burn any of the cities built on their mounds, except Hazor, which Joshua burned. Hazor is the one exception on that list. I'd call that a very specific detail.

The answer is nothing at all, friends. Verse 15 says Joshua did it all, "…leaving nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses." Moses, Israel's leader before Joshua, passed the command on, and Joshua carried it out. Picture a to-do list with every box checked.
The answer is False. Joshua 11:18 says he waged war against all these kings "…for a long period of time." So this wasn't wrapped up in a few days. Taking that whole region took a long stretch.

The answer is the Hivites of Gibeon, friends. Verse 19 says no city made peace with the Israelites except the Hivites living in Gibeon, and all others were taken in battle. Out of the whole region, one city made peace. That tells you how rare it was.

The answer is Gaza, Gath and Ashdod, friends! Verse 22 says no Anakim were left in the land of the Israelites, "only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod did any survive." Verse 21 has Joshua clearing them out of the hill country, and then this little list is all that's left. Three cities.

The answer is inheritance, friends. Verse 23 says Joshua "…gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to the allotments to their tribes." It's the kind of thing handed down, the way a family keeps the good recipe. The land was given out by allotments to the tribes.
